mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 4.5%, the S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which drives corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO below 100) indicates economic contraction, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO is below 100, the S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2.0% (computed from GDPC1) indicates robust economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When the quarterly GDP growth rate (from GDPC1) is above 2.0%, the S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% signals rising inflation, which typically leads to a hawkish monetary policy response and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL year-over-year growth exceeds 2.5%, the S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which typically leads to higher consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market downturn (HOUST below 1200 thousand units), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to reduced consumer confidence and spending, leading to negative returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST is below 1200, the S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.
